title: Hyderabad Engineer Uday Ruddarraju Named OpenAI's Chief Technology Officer of Compute
excerpt: The Indian-origin executive, who built xAI's Colossus supercomputer before joining OpenAI last year, will lead the infrastructure powering GPT-5.6 and future AI models.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Uday Ruddarraju has been appointed CTO of Compute at OpenAI, overseeing infrastructure for GPT-5.6.
  • He previously built xAI's Colossus supercomputer, one of the largest AI computing systems.
  • Ruddarraju's career includes roles at eBay, Robinhood, and Amazon Web Services.
  • His appointment highlights the rise of Indian-origin executives in global tech leadership.
  • Indian-origin engineer Uday Ruddarraju has been promoted to Chief Technology Officer of Compute at OpenAI, overseeing the infrastructure powering GPT-5.6 and future AI models.
  • Ruddarraju studied computer science at Hyderabad's Chaitanya Bharathi Institute of Technology before moving to the US for a master's degree at the University of Minnesota.
  • He previously built xAI's Colossus supercomputer — one of the largest AI computing systems ever constructed — before joining OpenAI in July 2025.
  • The appointment adds to a growing roster of Indian-origin executives leading the world's most influential technology companies.

OpenAI has promoted Indian-origin engineer Uday Ruddarraju to Chief Technology Officer of Compute, placing him in charge of the massive infrastructure required to train and deploy the company's frontier AI models. Ruddarraju announced the appointment on LinkedIn, describing his first year at the Microsoft-backed company as "incredibly rewarding."

From Hyderabad to the Heart of AI

Ruddarraju's path to one of the most closely watched roles in artificial intelligence began at Chaitanya Bharathi Institute of Technology (CBIT) in Hyderabad, where he earned his undergraduate degree in computer science. He interned at Amazon Web Services while still in college before moving to the United States for a master's degree at the University of Minnesota.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=SqfEXGdgQyQ

His professional career took him through eBay, where he worked from 2013 to 2018, and then to stock trading platform Robinhood. In 2024, he joined Elon Musk's AI venture xAI as Head of Infrastructure Engineering, where he led the construction of Colossus — a supercomputer housing over 250,000 GPUs and one of the largest AI computing systems ever built. He also oversaw the training of Grok 3, xAI's flagship model.

""Reporting into Elon and learning directly from him was definitely the best part about working at xAI," he wrote."

> **""Reporting into Elon and learning directly from him was definitely the best part about working at xAI," he wrote."**

Building the World's Largest Compute Footprint

As CTO of Compute, Ruddarraju will lead the systems that provide the enormous processing power needed to train models like GPT-5.6 and whatever comes next. In his LinkedIn post, he outlined the scale of the challenge ahead.

https://www.instagram.com/p/Da8M8hsG0B2/

"We're on a mission to build the world's largest compute footprint so frontier AI can reach everyone and every workflow. We have a very exciting compute ramp and roadmap coming up."

— Uday Ruddarraju, CTO of Compute, OpenAI

He noted that the compute team has worked to rapidly bring capacity online while strengthening the networking, storage, and machine learning systems underlying OpenAI's operations. The company is hiring across distributed systems, hardware engineering, manufacturing, and data centre construction spanning civil, mechanical, and electrical engineering.

Ruddarraju's departure from xAI in mid-2025 drew attention given his seniority and his central role in building the company's computing backbone. In a farewell message, he thanked Musk and the xAI team, calling it "a privilege to be part of a mission this bold."

https://x.com/indicanews1/status/2079348077568401565

He also spoke highly of working under Musk directly. "Reporting into Elon and learning directly from him was definitely the best part about working at xAI," he wrote. Referencing Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, he added: "Jensen Huang was right — Elon and his teams are singular in what they can achieve."

Part of a Broader Pattern

Ruddarraju's appointment extends a long and growing list of Indian-origin executives leading global technology companies. The most recent high-profile addition was CRED founder Kunal Shah, who was named global head and CEO of WhatsApp last month. The broader roster includes Satya Nadella at Microsoft, Sundar Pichai at Alphabet, Neal Mohan at YouTube, Arvind Krishna at IBM, and Nikesh Arora at Palo Alto Networks, among others.

At Anthropic, Bengaluru-raised Rahul Patil serves as CTO, and Vik Bajaj leads industrial AI startup Prometheus alongside Amazon founder Jeff Bezos. The trend reflects both the strength of India's engineering education pipeline and the competitive advantage that experience across multiple technical domains provides in the AI talent wars.

Building AI's Future
›Ruddarraju leads systems for GPT-5.6 and future models.
›OpenAI aims to build the world's largest compute footprint.
›Hiring across multiple engineering disciplines to support growth.
›Focus on networking, storage, and machine learning systems.

What's Next

With OpenAI racing to scale its infrastructure ahead of what Ruddarraju called a "very exciting compute ramp," his appointment signals the company's focus on the physical foundations of AI development. As competition intensifies between OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and xAI, the ability to build and operate compute at unprecedented scale has become as critical as the models themselves.
